turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just have this feeling like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, when we have our morning staff meetings for the maintenance crew—I clean buildings for a living, mostly the middle school over on 4th street. And my supervisor, Dave, he's a good guy, but he can talk for forty-five minutes straight about the new floor wax. I mean, wax is wax, right? Back in the 90s, we used this heavy-duty stuff that smelled like pure ammonia, but man, it made the linoleum shine like glass. You don't see that anymore with all the eco-friendly stuff they make us buy now. 

But yeah, during those meetings, or even at church event briefings on Sundays, I just can't sit there listening to it. I end up shifting around in my chair, standing up in the back, or I just find some excuse to go check a supply closet or empty a trash can just so I can move around.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes shifting around in his chair during meetings.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states he stands up in the back or finds excuses to leave his seat during meetings where he is expected to sit.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly describes feeling restless when supposed to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes feeling like he has a 'motor humming right under my skin' and constantly needing to move around.

turns.doctor_question: Going back to when you were a kid in school—did you have this same trouble sitting still in class, or is this something that's come up more recently as an adult?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, definitely. I remember getting in trouble way back in grade school for popping out of my seat all the time. I'd talk over the teacher, rush ahead before they even finished giving directions... my mother always used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even as a little kid. 

Speaking of my mother, she actually used to bake the most incredible apple pies. She had this secret recipe, something about using a mix of Granny Smith and Honeycrisp apples, and she'd put this little dash of cardamom in the crust. You wouldn't think cardamom belongs in an apple pie crust, but let me tell you, it gave it this warm, spicy kick that was just out of this world. She used to enter them in the county fair every summer. I think she won a blue ribbon back in '78 or '79. We still have the ribbon somewhere in a box in the attic, along with my old baseball cards. I had a whole collection of Topps cards from the 70s, mostly Mets players. Tom Seaver, man, what a pitcher. They don't make them like that anymore. 

But yeah, anyway, the sitting still thing... it's been there since I was a kid.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient recalls 'popping out of my seat all the time' during grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient mentions his mother described him as being 'wound too tight' as a child, indicating constant activity or being driven by a motor.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient describes rushing ahead before directions were finished, aligning with acting prematurely before completion.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient states he would 'talk over the teacher,' demonstrating interrupting or intruding on others.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality by going off on a long, unrelated tangent about apple pies and baseball cards before returning to the topic.

turns.doctor_question: When you're trying to focus on a task—like reading instructions, filling out paperwork, or listening to someone explain something important—do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you usually do okay with that part?
turns.patient_response:
Well, you know, it's funny you ask about reading instructions and paperwork and stuff. Honestly, I don't really have a problem with that part. I can read just fine, keep my head down and get through it if I have to. Like when I had to fill out all the tax forms last year—which, by the way, they changed the whole layout of the 1040 form again. It used to be you just followed the lines down, but now they've got all these schedules and worksheets. My buddy Al, he runs a hardware store over on Elm Street, he actually hired an accountant because he got so fed up with it. He sells these amazing custom birdhouses, though. Real craftsmanship. He uses cedar, mostly, so they last forever outside. I bought one for my wife a few years back and we get cardinals in the yard almost every morning now. Beautiful birds. 

But yeah, anyway, the focus thing... no, I don't really lose my attention when I'm doing that kind of stuff. It's more just the sitting still that gets me.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly states that 'sitting still' is what bothers him, indicating feelings of restlessness.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, rambling, and tangential story about tax forms, his friend's hardware store, and birdhouses, demonstrating excessive talking.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having trouble focusing or losing attention when doing tasks like reading instructions or paperwork.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned earlier that you used to talk over your teacher and rush ahead before getting directions. Do you still find yourself doing things like interrupting people when they're talking, or acting on impulses without thinking it through first?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do that all the time. Like, when Dave—my supervisor—or one of the folks at church starts giving me instructions for the day, I just jump right in. I'll blurt out what I think they're going to say before they even finish their sentence. And, you know, sometimes I get it wrong and they have to correct me, which is a little embarrassing. 

Speaking of the church, though, they just redid the landscaping out front. They put in these gorgeous azalea bushes. Have you ever tried growing azaleas? They can be really finicky about the soil pH. You need it to be pretty acidic. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has the most incredible garden. She uses pine needles as mulch to keep the acidity up. She's been living in that house for, gosh, must be forty years now. Her husband used to work at the old auto plant before it shut down in the early 2000s. It was a real shame when that place closed, a lot of good people lost their jobs. I remember the local diner used to be packed every day at lunchtime with guys from the plant. They had this meatloaf special on Thursdays... best meatloaf I ever had, hands down. It was all about the glaze they put on top, kind of sweet and tangy. 

But yeah, I definitely still interrupt people and jump the gun on things. It's just hard to wait for them to get to the point.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient demonstrates excessive talking by going on a long, unprompted tangent about landscaping, a neighbor, an auto plant, and meatloaf.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient explicitly states, 'I'll blurt out what I think they're going to say before they even finish their sentence.'
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient admits, 'I definitely still interrupt people and jump the gun on things.'

turns.doctor_question: When you're working—like cleaning the buildings or doing maintenance tasks—do you ever find yourself making careless mistakes, losing track of what you're supposed to be doing, or having trouble keeping organized with your work?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, I keep my cart organized and I know what I'm supposed to be doing. I've been doing it long enough, you know? It's pretty routine. You just go floor by floor, empty the trash, check the dispensers... speaking of the dispensers, they just switched us over to this new kind of paper towel at work. It's supposed to be more eco-friendly, made from recycled materials or whatever, but it's so thin it just falls apart in your hands when it's wet. It's like trying to dry your hands with a tissue. 

My wife buys those really nice, thick paper towels for the house. The kind with the quilted pattern on them? We go through a ton of them because of the dog. We have this golden retriever mix, Buster, and he is just a mess. Sweetest dog in the world, but he tracks mud in every time it rains. And let me tell you, it's been raining buckets lately. We had a storm roll through last Tuesday that knocked out the power for three hours. I had to go dig out the old camping lantern from the garage. I love that lantern, it's one of those old Coleman ones that runs on white gas. My dad gave it to me when I moved out. We used to go camping up in the state park every summer when I was a kid. We'd catch trout in the river and cook them right there over the fire. 

But yeah, mistakes at work? No, I'm pretty good about keeping on track with all that. The cleaning part is fine.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, rambling response detailing unrelated topics like paper towels, his dog, and childhood camping trips, demonstrating excessive talking.
symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly denies making careless mistakes at work.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient denies losing track of tasks, stating he knows what he is supposed to be doing and keeps on track.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly denies having trouble with organization, noting he keeps his work cart organized.

turns.doctor_question: When you're doing something you find interesting or enjoyable—like a hobby or something you really like—do you have trouble keeping your mind on it, or do you stay focused pretty well with those kinds of things?
turns.patient_response:
No, if it's something I actually like doing, I'm totally fine. I can stay on it for hours. Like, I love tinkering with old radios. You know, the big wooden ones from the thirties and forties? I've got this beautiful Philco model out in the garage right now. I've been trying to find a replacement vacuum tube for it, which is getting harder and harder these days. You have to scour these online forums, and half the time the guys selling them want an arm and a leg. 

There's this one guy in Ohio, though, who has a whole warehouse full of them. I think his name is Stan. He actually invited me out there once to take a look, but I haven't had the time to make the drive. Ohio's a beautiful state, though, especially in the fall. My wife's sister lives out near Cleveland, and we went out for Thanksgiving a couple years back. They deep-fried the turkey, which I thought was crazy, but it was actually the juiciest turkey I've ever had. You have to be really careful, though, because if the turkey isn't completely thawed out, the oil will just explode everywhere. I saw a video of that happening on the news once, it burned the guy's whole deck down. 

But no, to answer your question, if I'm doing something I enjoy, I don't lose focus at all. I'm locked right in.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, rambling response that goes off on multiple tangents (radios, Ohio, Thanksgiving, deep-fried turkeys) before returning to the question, demonstrating excessive talking.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having trouble sustaining attention on enjoyable tasks, stating they can stay focused for hours and are 'locked right in'.
